answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks over an attestation graph, so voting weight reflects paths reachable from trusted roots rather than identities alone. A sybil cluster joined to honest nodes by a sparse external cut has low conductance: few walk transitions cross its boundary, limiting the trust mass it can accrue within the walk budget. Under fixed roots and weighting rules, this bounds its aggregate voting weight; violet marks, spiral paths, and nadir scores do not bypass the cut.
